title: add jsonschema strict response_format + openai compatibility for structured output
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds response_format=json_schema support with an optional strict mode that validates model output against a provided JSON Schema. Default behavior is backward-compatible (non-strict). Includes OpenAI-compat param passthrough and docs. Rollout gated by feature flag.
description:
Motivation: Add first-class JSON Schema structured output support to the public API and OpenAI-compat layer so customers can declare a schema and get validated, machine-friendly responses. Include a strict mode that enforces schema conformance and returns structured validation errors so product teams can decide whether to treat schema violations as errors or fallbacks.

What this PR does: Implements a 'response_format' API parameter that accepts a JSON Schema payload and a 'strict' boolean. In non-strict mode we attempt model-first generation and validate the final output; on failure we return the best-effort output plus a validation block. In strict mode the service validates the final output and returns a structured ValidationError with code and context when the output does not conform. We also add an OpenAI-compat compatibility shim so clients using the OpenAI-style response_format schema (tools/function-calling compatibility) get equivalent behavior.

Implementation notes: - New JSON Schema validator module (service/validation/jsonschema_validator.go) using our internal fast-jsonschema runtime with precompiled schemas for common patterns and a fallback to the slower validator. - Wire up response_format parsing in the API layer (service/api/response_format.go), and propagate validation results through the response envelope. - Streaming: to avoid partial-stream ambiguity when strict=true we buffer the first response chunk and run a lightweight validation on the generated prefix before flushing; for non-strict streaming behavior is unchanged but we emit a validation metadata frame at the end. - OpenAI compatibility: add openai-compat/response_format_shim.go to translate OpenAI-style JSON Schema + function-calling hints into our response_format. - Errors: introduce structured error codes (VALIDATION_FAILED, SCHEMA_PARSE_ERROR) and human-readable messages with a 'validation_details' object describing failing paths and example corrections. - Observability: add metrics response_format.requests, response_format.strict_failures, response_format.validation_latency_ms.

Testing: Unit tests for validator and API layer added, integration test exercising strict and non-strict streaming paths, OpenAI-compat roundtrip tests, and e2e against a small local LLM stub. CI run initially showed an intermittent streaming e2e flake; I reran the job and it passed. All green on merge.

Backward compatibility and rollout: Default remains non-strict. 'strict' must be opt-in. We gated the feature behind a feature flag (deploy/feature_flags.json) and plan a staged rollout: internal canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over two weeks, monitoring response_format.strict_failures and downstream customer errors. No breaking changes to existing clients.

Open questions / follow-ups: - Add an automatic schema-suggestion utility that generates approximate schema from sample outputs (followup ENG-2199). - Docs: add a migration guide for customers that want to opt-in to strict mode and to handle validation errors (done in docs but we'll expand examples).

Related tickets: ENG-2145, ENG-2199, SUP-487.
